title: MMS, homogeneous natural (do-nothing) outlet per viscous form, with a field built for each form
physics: Field sq_do_nothing_lap has (mu G - pI) n = 0 on x=1 but (2 mu eps - pI) n != 0; field sq_do_nothing_sym the reverse. Each is solved with its own form.

solver.tight: same, plus 2 steps of iterative refinement (vacuous for a direct solve; meaningful only for an iterative solver)

parameters.pressure_constant_treatment: the residual reported is that of the consistent system solved; the measured flux defect is reported

structured.construction: f1a_stokes_check.structured_mesh(N): the N = 8 BASE mesh (8 x 8 squares split along the (1,1) diagonal, except the two cells at the corners (1,0) and (0,1), split the other way: no triangle with all vertices on the boundary) refined uniformly (red) log2(N/8) times. Nested; the flipped region of level N is a (N/8) x (N/8) block at each of those corners. The check module verifies counts, hash and nestedness.
structured.h_definition: h_nominal = 1/N (leg of the right triangles); h_max = sqrt(2)/N reported too

boundaries.x1: do-nothing (no data: the natural condition of the form)

parameters.shared_node_rule: At a velocity node shared by several boundary attributes: (1) Dirichlet beats every natural condition (traction, do-nothing) and every slip/symmetry constraint (the slip constraint is not imposed at such nodes); (2) between Dirichlet attributes the fixed data AGREE at shared nodes (checked: dirichlet_shared_node_mismatch_max), so no precedence between them is needed and the result is independent of attribute order; (3) between two slip/symmetry attributes both normal constraints are imposed (u = 0 at a convex corner); (4) a periodic pair at a Dirichlet corner takes the (periodic-consistent) Dirichlet value.

convergence.norm: ||u - u_h||_L2(Omega): element quadrature of degree 10 (exact u at the quadrature points; no interpolation of the exact solution)
|u - u_h|_H1(Omega) seminorm (all four components of grad), degree-10 quadrature
||p_h - p||_L2(Omega), no mean removal (pressure determined by the boundary data / constraint)
